state_doh_release.mode:
Mississippi State Department of Health Authorizes Expanded Syringe Services Program Coverage
The Department has approved expansion of authorized syringe services programs to additional counties under Mississippi public health authority. Syringe services programs reduce transmission of HIV and hepatitis C, connect individuals to medication for opioid use disorder, and distribute naloxone and fentanyl test strips. Decades of peer-reviewed evidence and CDC guidance support syringe services programs as a core component of the public health response to drug-related harms.

key_findings: 3 columns have missing values; highest is state_doh_release (29.6%).

residual_analysis.heteroscedasticity_note: strong positive — errors grow with predicted values

schema_comparison.note: 0 column(s) only in training data (may include target components); 1 column(s) only in prediction data.

target_distribution.interpretation: heavily right-skewed — log-transform of target may help

shifted_features.note: notable upward trend in pred; prefer lag/difference features over raw level

cross_feature_target_patterns.note: No low-cardinality numeric x time interaction patterns detected.

recommendations: Prediction rows are temporally after training rows: use time-based holdout (hold out last 20% of training timestamps) rather than random split.
Target is right-skewed (skewness=2.70): consider log-transform; MAE on raw target will weight large values heavily.

lag_features.rationale: All four lags show strong within-group autocorrelation (lag1=0.562, lag3=0.521, lag6=0.465, lag12=0.422). Per-group series length is uniformly 77 periods (min=77 >= 3x12=36), so lag12 is well-supported. Rolling windows sized to match lag horizons. gtrends_fentanyl and gtrends_naloxone show distribution shift in pred; use lag/difference features rather than raw levels for these.

distribution_shift_caution: gtrends_fentanyl: train_mean=51.8, pred_mean=68.8 — prefer lag/diff features
gtrends_naloxone: train_mean=47.0, pred_mean=64.2 — prefer lag/diff features
unemployment_rate: 54.6% missing in pred — impute with jurisdiction-level last-known or median
labor_force: 58.0% missing in pred — impute with jurisdiction-level last-known or median
